records.title: Introduction to Asian Languages and Literature
records.header: ASIAN 200 Introduction to Asian Languages and Literature (5) A&H
records.text: ASIAN 200 Introduction to Asian Languages and Literature (5) A&H Introduces approaches to the study of Asian languages and literature. Topics include theoretical, applied, historical, and comparative linguistics; literary and cultural study; philosophy; languages, and writing systems of Asia; and indigenous Asian approaches to the study of language and literature. Offered: Sp.

records.title: Asian War Epics: Working through Many Mahabharatas
records.header: ASIAN 210 Asian War Epics: Working through Many Mahabharatas (5) A&H/SSc
records.text: ASIAN 210 Asian War Epics: Working through Many Mahabharatas (5) A&H/SSc Culturally informed aesthetic analysis, comparisons of different tellings of parallel scenes (both South and Southeast Asian). Includes classical and contemporary retellings, and representation in socio-political discourse, visual arts, musical dance, drama, and in popular media such as film and television. In English translation.

records.title: Languages and Cultures of China
records.header: ASIAN 211 Languages and Cultures of China (5) A&H/SSc
records.text: ASIAN 211 Languages and Cultures of China (5) A&H/SSc Provides a general survey of the languages and language-families in China, emphasizing the rich linguistic diversity found there today. Languages compared with English, from linguistic and cultural perspectives, to demonstrate not only characteristics but also mutual dependence throughout their development.

records.title: Buddhist Literature
records.text: ASIAN 223 Buddhist Literature (5) A&H/SSc Introduction to Buddhist literature in India, China, and Japan including biographies, poetry, narratives, ritual manuals, doctrinal treatises, and historical accounts. Attention also given to issues of textual composition, transmission, authorship, audience, context, and function. Taught in English. Offered: W.

records.title: Confucius: Ideas That Shaped East Asia
records.header: ASIAN 224 Confucius: Ideas That Shaped East Asia (5) A&H
records.text: ASIAN 224 Confucius: Ideas That Shaped East Asia (5) A&H Explores one of the most influential philosophers in world history, Confucius (551-479 BCE), who has shaped East Asian civilizations and remains influential today. Traces the intellectual strains from the time before Confucius down to the present day.

records.title: Great Works of Asian Literature
records.header: ASIAN 263 Great Works of Asian Literature (5) A&H
records.text: ASIAN 263 Great Works of Asian Literature (5) A&H Selected major works of Asian literature. Taught on a rotational basis with the literary traditions of China, Japan, India covered in successive years. Content varies depending on specialization and interest of instructor. Primary emphasis on literary values of works and their tradition; attention also given to historical and social contexts and the thought and value systems of the culture involved.

records.header: ASIAN 301 Songs of the Saints of India (5) A&H/SSc
records.text: ASIAN 301 Songs of the Saints of India (5) A&H/SSc India's wisdom through popular songs of its saints of the devotional tradition. Texts as significant in contemporary religion and politics, whether protesting existing hierarchies of caste and gender, or confirming the status quo. Readings in English translation.

records.title: Introduction to Asian Linguistics
records.header: ASIAN 401 Introduction to Asian Linguistics (5) A&H
records.text: ASIAN 401 Introduction to Asian Linguistics (5) A&H Linguistic analysis, with emphasis on languages of East, Southeast, South, and Central Asia. Includes phonetics, phonemics, morphology, syntax, historical reconstruction, linguistic typology, comparative grammar. Survey of major languages and language families of Asia. Diverse Asian languages as subjects of linguistic analysis. Prior knowledge of linguistics not required.

records.title: Writing Systems
records.text: ASIAN 404 Writing Systems (5) A&H Comprehensive theoretical and historical overview of written language worldwide. Includes origins and early development of writing in the Near East, Asia, and the Americas; relationships between spoken and written languages; types and characteristic of writing systems (logographics, syllabic, and alphabetic); and methods used for decipherment of ancient languages. Offered: W.

records.header: ASIAN 405 Advanced Problems in Asian Linguistics (3) A&H
records.text: ASIAN 405 Advanced Problems in Asian Linguistics (3) A&H Advanced problems in the analysis of the languages of East, Southeast, South, and Central Asia. Includes phonology, morphology, syntax, lexicography, historical reconstruction, linguistic typology, and comparative grammar. Prerequisite: ASIAN 401.

records.title: Computational Text Analysis for Asian Language Material
records.header: ASIAN 413 Computational Text Analysis for Asian Language Material (5) A&H, RSN
records.text: ASIAN 413 Computational Text Analysis for Asian Language Material (5) A&H, RSN Students learn to understand, organize, analyze, interpret, and visualize Asian cultural and literary texts as data using computational methods. Emphasizes methodologies in computational text analysis and text mining, network analysis, algorithmic reading, and programming, focusing on Asian language material and the specifics posed by these languages.

records.title: Internship in Teaching Asian Languages and Cultures
records.header: ASIAN 491 Internship in Teaching Asian Languages and Cultures (1-2, max. 5)
records.text: ASIAN 491 Internship in Teaching Asian Languages and Cultures (1-2, max. 5) Teaching internship in a language course (undergrad or grad students are eligible) or a disciplinary course (graduate students only), as arranged with the supervising instructor. Faculty permission required. 3 hr/week internship earns 1 credit, 6 hr/week internship earns 2 credits. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSpS.

records.title: Ramayana in Comparative Perspective
records.header: ASIAN 494 Ramayana in Comparative Perspective (5) A&H, DIV
records.text: ASIAN 494 Ramayana in Comparative Perspective (5) A&H, DIV Examines and compares different versions (mainly South Asian) of the Ramayana, including the widely popular television version. Focuses on some famous and controversial passages, with special attention to gender issues. Incorporates background readings from the most recent research. Offered: jointly with JSIS A 461.
